title: Zebra stripes with :nth-child
summary: :nth-child(even) shades every other row; :hover highlights the row under the pointer.
explanation: :nth-child(even) matches the 2nd, 4th, 6th… child of its parent, so the stripes stay correct however many rows there are, with no extra classes in the HTML.
Pseudo-classes describe state as well as position. :hover applies while the pointer is over the row. It comes after the stripe rule and has the same specificity, so it wins on striped rows too.
Other useful patterns: :nth-child(3n) every third, :nth-child(-n + 3) the first three, :nth-child(odd) the others.
tryThis: Change it to 3n: every third row is shaded.
Move the :hover rule above the :nth-child rule: hovering a shaded row no longer changes it, because now the stripe comes later.
